sets.relationshipLabel: a worker and the tool of their trade
sets.explanation: A sugarmaker boils sap in an evaporator just as a gardener starts seedlings in a cold frame — each pair names a tradesperson and the instrument that defines their craft.

sets.relationshipLabel: the thing that stops the other from happening
sets.explanation: A row cover keeps frost off tender plants and a windbreak keeps snow from drifting where it's unwanted — each first word exists specifically to block the second.

sets.relationshipLabel: a category and a named kind within it
sets.explanation: An onion snow is a named kind of flurry, just as a robin snow is a named kind of shower — folk names nested inside the general weather category.

sets.relationshipLabel: a sign and what it announces
sets.explanation: Skunk cabbage pushing through means mud season has arrived, and pussy willows budding mean the sap run has begun — each plant is nature's herald for the season it precedes.

glossary.definition: A light, late snowfall that surprises everyone after the weather has already turned mild in spring.

definitions.definition: Someone who taps trees and boils the sap down into syrup each spring.
A big flat pan set over heat that boils sap down until it turns into syrup.
Someone who grows plants and vegetables, tending them from seed to harvest.
A low box with a clear top that shelters young plants and warms the soil early in the season.
A lightweight fabric laid over plants to shield them from cold nights.
A thin icy coating that forms on cold nights and can damage tender plants.
A line of trees or a fence built to slow the wind and protect what's behind it.
A mound of snow piled up by the wind against something in its path.
A brief, light burst of snow that comes and goes quickly.
A light, late snowfall that surprises everyone after the weather has already turned mild in spring.
A short spell of rain that passes through and then clears up.
A light spring snowfall that comes right around the time robins return.
An early spring plant with a strong smell that pushes up through half-frozen ground.
The messy, thawing stretch between winter and spring when the ground turns soft and wet.
A shrub with soft, fuzzy buds that appear in very early spring.
The stretch of days when sap flows freely up through maple trees, ready for tapping.
